transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net broadband technical operations, my name is Oscar. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Oscar, my name is Talia Brooks. We pay for your Ultrafast 500 Mbps fiber broadband, but over the past week our connection has been fluctuating wildly: one minute it tests at 480 Mbps and the next minute it plunges to 2 Mbps, dropping my work Zoom meetings and making remote working impossible!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon Talia. If I understand correctly, your Ultrafast 500 Mbps broadband is experiencing severe speed instability, fluctuating dramatically between 480 Mbps and 2 Mbps and causing continuous drops during your remote video meetings. Before we inspect your optical network terminal and line telemetry, could you please confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 18 Hawthorne Road, Cheltenham, GL50 2DN, security PIN 6592, router model S-Net Hub 5.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Talia, that confirms your account details. Have you noticed if the speed drops occur at specific times of day or when certain household devices connect?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It happens completely randomly throughout the day, even when only a single laptop is connected via Ethernet cable.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could I place you on hold for two minutes while I query your Optical Network Terminal optical power levels and continuous packet error telemetry?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Talia. Examining the optical line telemetry, your downstream optical receive power fluctuates between minus 16 dBm and minus 29 dBm.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does a fluctuation to minus 29 dBm indicate?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The optimal optical window is minus 15 to minus 22 dBm; when the signal drops to minus 29 dBm, the light level is near total optical extinction, causing massive frame drop and speed collapse.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What would cause the optical light level to swing so wildly?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It typically indicates a contaminated fiber optical connector or a micro-bend stress fracture on the external drop cable between the telegraph pole and your house.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you clean or repair the optical cable remotely?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Physical optical light fluctuations require an Openreach specialized fiber field engineer to clean the SC/APC bulkhead connector and re-splice the fiber joint.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How quickly can a fiber engineer attend our property?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can book a priority Openreach fiber repair engineer for tomorrow morning between eight and one o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Tomorrow morning would be fantastic.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously physical optical light loss requires precision laser re-splicing equipment that cannot be fixed by software reboots.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I understand that hardware light levels require physical attention.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: In the meantime, I can optimize your Hub 5 downstream channel bonding to stabilize the packets as much as possible.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please do that right away.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Talia speaking, I am the lead legal counsel for a major medical device corporation, and tomorrow afternoon at two o'clock I am chairing a critical transatlantic patent litigation hearing with international judges and opposing QC barristers! If my internet collapses during that hearing, our multimillion-pound medical patent could be invalidated and my professional career will be permanently ruined! I am in complete sheer panic and anxiety!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am querying the optical power levels and Openreach emergency dispatch slots right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please do Oscar, my transatlantic patent hearing is at two o'clock tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand the immense pressure, acute professional anxiety, and enormous career stakes of your transatlantic patent hearing tomorrow afternoon, Talia. While our engineering SLA cannot guarantee an on-site fiber laser repair engineer this evening, I will book the earliest first-slot engineer appointment for tomorrow morning at eight o'clock and dispatch our emergency 4G mobile broadband backup dongle so you have guaranteed dual-path connectivity before two o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Oscar! Having the engineer at eight in the morning and a 4G backup dongle gives me complete safety.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am booking the Openreach engineer slot under priority reference FBR-ENG-44910-C.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: FBR-ENG-44910-C, noted down.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The engineer will arrive between 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM and has notes to test both the external splice and the internal ONT connector.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will give them plenty of time before my two o'clock hearing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have also arranged for our local courier to deliver an S-Net 4G Mobile Backup USB Dongle to your door by 11:00 AM tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A courier delivery by 11:00 AM? Oscar, that is exceptional service!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The dongle plugs directly into the rear USB port of your Hub 5 and provides automatic instantaneous cellular failover.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So even if the fiber drops for a second, the 4G takes over without disconnecting Zoom?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly: the Hub 5 maintains stateful TCP sessions across the 4G tunnel without dropping active video calls.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is an extraordinary relief. I can sleep peacefully tonight.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have waived all engineering callout charges and courier delivery fees on your account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Oscar, you have gone above and beyond.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have documented your legal hearing deadline on the master incident log.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you for taking my situation so seriously.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our priority is ensuring our customers can work with complete confidence.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You have restored my faith in S-Net today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Best of luck with your patent litigation hearing tomorrow afternoon, Talia.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you so much Oscar.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we conclude, what was that Cheltenham postal address again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I told you right at the start of our call, it is 18 Hawthorne Road, Cheltenham.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Talia, the address is verified on the engineer job sheet.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you again Oscar for your compassionate and urgent help.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has been my pleasure assisting you, Talia. Have a wonderful evening.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Oscar.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other broadband technical issue I can assist with today, Talia?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No Oscar, that covers everything.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net broadband technical operations, Talia. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Oscar.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.text: Goodbye.
